ads_ratio.reason: Kinross is a direct-listed foreign private issuer: one NYSE-traded KGC share is one common share, so no ADS conversion applies; per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis.
ads_ratio.source: Form 40-F filed 2026-03-26 (CIK 701818): 'Our common shares are listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange' — the NYSE security is the common share itself, not an ADS; the _system README v5.3 note likewise lists KGC among the direct-listed ordinary-share filers (ratio 1.0)

moat_against: Pure gold price-taker: no pricing power; the 2025-26 earnings surge is the gold price (Q2 2026 realized $4,483/oz, +37% YoY), not volume — production fell 4% YoY
Finite, depleting reserves: ounces must be continually replaced with capex (2026 attributable capex guided ~$1,500M) just to hold production flat at ~2.0M oz/yr
Cost inflation erodes the price windfall: Q2 2026 AISC +22% YoY to $1,821/oz, production cost of sales +25% YoY (fuel, royalties, labor)
Jurisdictional and single-asset risk across Mauritania (Tasiast), Brazil, Chile and the US; permitting and tax/royalty regimes sit outside management's control
moat_for: Scale and diversification: ~2.0M Au eq. oz/yr guided production across mines in the US, Canada, Brazil, Mauritania and Chile — no single mine is the whole company
Net-cash balance sheet (engine: net debt -$1,004.1M at FY2025; $1.9B net cash at Q2 2026) with no debt maturities until 2033 per the Q2 2026 release — survives a gold downturn without distress
Development pipeline that can replace reserves: Great Bear (Canada) and Lobo-Marte (NPV $4.3B at a $4,100 gold price, per Q2 2026 release)
Capital discipline at current prices: buybacks plus dividends returned ~40% of free cash flow year-to-date 2026; share count shrinking ~1.8%/yr (engine share CAGR)
moat_justification: A gold miner is a price-taker on a depleting asset: Kinross has no pricing power, its reserves deplete and must be rebought with heavy capex, and cost inflation (+22% AISC YoY in Q2 2026) claws back price windfalls. What it does have is scale (~2.0M oz/yr across five countries), a net-cash balance sheet, and a real development pipeline (Great Bear, Lobo-Marte) — enough for a weak 3/10, not a durable moat.
name: Kinross Gold Corporation
one_liner: Solid, net-cash senior gold producer, moat 3/10 (price-taker on a depleting asset) — at $22.24 the price capitalizes peak-gold earnings: on the normalized median base with volume-realistic growth, weighted IRR is 8.8% and weighted IV@15 is $10.85; clears 15% only below ~$10.85.
